newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open stronger on U.S. retail data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open stronger on U.S. retail data.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened stronger on Tuesday, as a weaker-than-expected retail sales report spurred expectations that U.S. interest rates will not rise next week, dealers said.

"The retail sales number was really good out of the States," said one T-bill dealer with a bank-owned brokerage. "The market's focusing on the fact that now the Fed might not have to go on May 20. That's really what's driving the market."
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.03 percent from 3.05 percent at Monday's close.

Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets strengthened on Tuesday after the U.S. Commerce Department said retail sales fell 0.3 percent in April and fell 0.1 percent less auto sales. Sales were expected to fall 0.3 percent overall and rise 0.1 percent less auto sales.

The report was seen as reducing the likelihood that the U.S. Federal Reserve would hike rates at next week's meeting of its Open Market Committee. A U.S. rate hike would likely weaken the Canadian money market and currency.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.40 percent from 3.43 percent on Monday.
The one-year T-bill firmed to yield 3.93 percent from 3.98 percent.
The call loan rate traded at 3.0 percent, in the center of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.

In new issue news, the Bank of Canada this afternoon will auction C$4.3 billion of three-month, six-month, and one-year T-bills, even as C$5.1 billion in T-bills mature. Results of the auction will be announced at 1315 EDT/1715 GMT.
